newsitem.title: USA: U.S. exporters report wheat sales to Egypt, unknown.
newsitem.headline: U.S. exporters report wheat sales to Egypt, unknown.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said private exporters reported sales of 110,000 tonnes of hard red winter wheat to Egypt for delivery during the 1997/98 marketing year and 110,000 tonnes of hard red winter wheat to unknown destinations for delivery in 1997/98.

U.S. exporters also reported purchases from foreign sellers of 110,000 tonnes of hard red winter wheat for delivery to unknown destinations during the 1997/98 marketing year. A purchase from a foreign seller is a transaction in which a U.S. exporter contracts to buy U.S. produced commodities from a foreign firm, USDA said.

The marketing year for wheat began June 1. Exporters must report to USDA sales of 100,000 tonnes or more of one commodity made in one day to a single destination by 1500 ET the next business day after the sale. Sales of lesser quantities must be reported weekly.
